sources.name: OGC Web Coverage Service (WCS) 2.1 Interface Standard - Core
sources.role: coverage retrieval, core operations and extension-bound response contract
verified_facts: WCS provides Internet access to multidimensional coverage data representing space/time-varying phenomena.
WCS 2.1 extends WCS 2.0 backwards-compatibly to support CIS 1.1 coverages in addition to CIS 1.0.
The core defines mandatory service requirements, while additional extensions are required to completely specify response encodings and optional capabilities.
semantic_limits: A successful WCS response or core conformance claim does not independently validate terrain accuracy, parcel geometry or vertical datum.
GetCoverage output remains fail-closed until coverage identity, source version, encoding, CRS, units and complete payload are verified.
Service availability and HTTP success must not create a business row.

sources.name: OGC Coverage Implementation Schema 1.1.1
sources.role: coverage envelope, domain, range, range-type, axis-order and partition contract
verified_facts: A concrete coverage structure contains an envelope, domainSet, rangeSet and rangeType, with optional metadata.
Direct-position coordinate order follows the axis order of the CRS defined by the coverage context.
CIS supports multiple encodings and partitioned coverages whose components may be stored or referenced separately.
semantic_limits: A coverage envelope is a bounding construct and is not proof of exact HMLR parcel containment.
rangeType describes value structure and semantics; it is not the range values themselves.
A partition reference or partial component is not proof that the complete coverage range was read.

sources.name: OGC CF-netCDF 3.0 encoding using GML Coverage Application Schema
sources.role: CF-netCDF domain, coordinate-system, range and remote-value reference contract
verified_facts: The standard maps CF-netCDF datasets and coordinate variables to concrete GML coverage domain, coverageFunction, rangeType and rangeSet structures.
Only spatial and temporal coordinates become part of the coverage CRS; parametric dimensions can be represented as range components.
A service response may carry binary values, XML metadata, multipart attachments or a Web address, but its content must remain consistent with the coverage model.
semantic_limits: A Web address or ncML metadata document is not evidence that all referenced binary values were downloaded and checked.
Coordinate-system mapping does not independently establish ODN vertical datum, units or source accuracy.
A parametric axis or CF variable mapping is not a parcel height-difference measurement.

sources.name: OGC GML Application Schema - Coverages JPEG2000 Coverage Encoding Extension
sources.role: JPEG2000 dimensions, CRS, axis, cell geometry, component-order and reduced-resolution contract
verified_facts: JPEG2000 coverage encoding is limited to supported two-dimensional GML coverage types.
CRS, axis ordering, cell geometry and range-component ordering must remain consistent across GML and any embedded encoding.
JPEG2000 can expose reduced resolution, reduced quality or reduced spatial regions from portions of the compressed codestream.
semantic_limits: A reduced-resolution, reduced-quality or spatially cropped decode is not full-resolution numeric terrain evidence.
JPEG2000 format conformance does not establish source authority, vertical datum or parcel measurement accuracy.
Because distribution of the GML description with the JPEG2000 file is outside this standard's scope, pairing and content integrity require separate verification.
